notes: Fiftieth daf of the campaign. Started as a rashi-repair attempt (only 18/60 lines were scaffold-baselined with the 'continues/concludes' narration pattern; the docs table's task recommendation was rashi-reconstruction based on rule composition, but drift was ALIGNED and I initially judged repair proportionate). Generated a repair manifest and packet, then inspected the packet's Current rashiTranslations closely before writing anything: found that lines 34-60 (27 of 60 lines, spanning six real Gemara segments l34/l36/l41's worth of content) were ALL linked to the single id l34, even though l36 and l41 are separate legal ids with their own real Gemara text further along -- a severe positional-collapse mislinking defect the scaffold-prefix detector cannot see (it only flags narration style, not link correctness). Also found lines 3-4 linked to l03 despite l03 (and l06) carrying zero independent comments per a live Sefaria cross-check. Given roughly half the daf's linking was wrong regardless of narration style, switched from rashi-repair to rashi-reconstruction and did a full ground-up reconstruction of all 60 lines against the 11-id local segment table (l01, l03, l06, l10, l16, l21, l25, l30, l34, l36, l41), fully superseding the repair attempt. Live-fetched Rashi_on_Yoma.44a from the Sefaria API v3 (11 LINE positions) as boundary-truth cross-reference; the 11 Sefaria positions map 1:1 in order to the packet's 11 local ids, confirming l03 and l06 both genuinely carry zero independent comments (Sefaria's own empty array entries at those positions) and that l34 itself has only one short dibbur ('mai lav khu - kedeparishit'), with l36 and l41 each carrying their own substantial, previously-uncaptured content. The final raw line ('bekedushah', a complete word but a truncated dibbur hamatchil) was confirmed via modules/yoma/assets/talmuddev/44b.json's first raw Rashi line ('bekedushah. matan damim: sham perishah achat...') to be the genuine start of Rashi's next comment continuing onto 44b; linked to l41, this daf's final local id, per established boundary policy. First-pass drift profile was ALIGNED but with both anchors at offset +1 (not 0), which worker:verify's fast pass flagged as 2 semantic-audit shift candidates and worker:review correctly failed on drift-profile-ALIGNED and semantic-audit-zero-shift-candidates (the multi-anchor evidence tier requires offsets exactly 0). Root-caused this to a genuine off-by-one line-assignment bug of my own: raw line 2 ends with 'lekamei mefaresh' (further on it explains) which is the tail of l01's comment plus the opening of l10's comment, but my first-pass translation had absorbed that phrase entirely into line 3's entry, silently shifting every subsequent line's content one position early relative to its actual raw-Hebrew line for the rest of the daf (the (Numbers 17) citation on raw line 6 ended up in my line 7's translation, and (47a) on raw line 25 ended up in line 26). Fully rebuilt the line-by-line split from raw line 1 onward with each entry matching only its own raw line's actual words, verified byte-exact against modules/yoma/assets/talmuddev/44a.json; the two citations now land on their correct lines (6 and 25) and audit_rashi_semantic.profile_daf('44a') confirms both offsets are exactly 0 post-fix, 2/2 anchors found, ALIGNED. This is exactly the kind of self-caught, gate-driven correction the pipeline is designed to force before merge; worker:verify --fast and worker:review were both re-run clean after the fix and reported zero shift candidates. Every raw-line English was checked against its byte-exact source line via direct dictionary lookup in the build script and a full visual reread of all 60 printed HE/EN pairs against the packet and the Sefaria cross-check. audit_rashi_scaffold.py 44a --no-baseline reports 0 hits after rebuild; baseline 3254 -> 3236 via --update-baseline, verified the 18 retired entries are exclusively daf=44a with zero additions or rehashes elsewhere. No repetition-baseline or content-allowlist entry existed for 44a before or after. audit_rashi_association.py --range-from 44a --range-to 44a: 67 declared associations, 0 broken, 0 cross-daf, single_link=53, multi_link=7. Diff scope is exactly the 8 expected files (VERSION, target learning.json, learning_data.js, the scaffold-debt baseline, docs/rashi-audit-backlog.md, package.json/package-lock.json, plus this self-review and the manifest) with no unauthorized files touched.
